newsitem.title: NEPAL: United States pledges $30 million aid to Nepal.
newsitem.headline: United States pledges $30 million aid to Nepal.

text.p: The United States pledged on Friday $30 million in non-refundable grants spread over five years for Nepal's agriculture and health projects, Finance Ministry officials said.

They said the U.S. aid included $25 million to raise the output of high-value forest and agricultural products like timber and non-timber items, livestock, fruits, vegetables, seeds, species and processed goods.
A statement by the United States Information Service said the aid would also support privatisation of the Himalayan kingdom's state-owned agriculture and forest-based enterprises.
The aid includes another $5 million for the control of AIDS through increased condom use, and maternity and child health projects.
Nepal is one of the world's 10 poorest countries. More than 60 percent of its economic development costs are funded by Western donors.

Nepali officials said Washington would help Nepal reduce the mortality rate of children below the age of five to 85 per 1,000 live births from the 118 at present, and the total fertility rate to 4.0 children per woman in 2002 from 4.6 in 1996.
